headline: Neighbors already recommend you. Google hasn't met you yet.
summary: BME General Remodels is an owner-run remodel shop in Lemon Grove, the kind of local shop neighbors pass along when they need kitchens, bathrooms, drywall, or painting. On Nextdoor you were named a Neighborhood Favorite in 2024 and again in 2025, and you've been answering neighbor requests, including a reply in February 2025. The biggest leftover is Google. We couldn't find a Google listing for BME General Remodels at all, so anyone who searches Google for a Lemon Grove remodeler finds other shops instead. A free Google Business Profile, set up as a service-area business so a home address stays private, would give that reputation a clear place to land. Your Nextdoor hours are already posted, 6 AM to 6 PM Monday through Friday, 6 AM to 4 PM Saturday, and closed Sunday, so those can carry over to Google once the listing is up. One smaller thing to settle first: the name shows up a few ways, BME General Remodels on the page, BME General Construction in your own story, and BME General remodels Inc in a reply. Picking one spelling before the listing goes up will keep the name consistent.

signals.note: When we searched Google's business listings for BME General Remodels in Lemon Grove, nothing came back for you. Other remodel shops showed up, but they were different businesses. Your Nextdoor page is clearly working, including Neighborhood Favorite nods in 2024 and 2025. Customers who aren't on Nextdoor have no way to find you.
signals.next: Set up a free Google Business Profile as a service-area business, so a home address stays private, and list Lemon Grove and the nearby areas you cover. Use the name you want to be known by, and pick categories that match the work you actually take on.

signals.note: Your number, (619) 846-7444, is on your Nextdoor page, and that's a solid place for neighbors to reach you. A referred customer can call you on the first try.
signals.next: Keep (619) 846-7444 as the single number everywhere, including a new Google listing.

signals.note: Your Nextdoor page already lists hours: 6 AM to 6 PM Monday through Friday, 6 AM to 4 PM Saturday, and closed Sunday. That's helpful. A neighbor can tell when it's a good time to call.
signals.next: Use the same hours on your Google listing once it is up, so the two places match.

signals.note: Without a Google listing, there's no place for searchers to see examples of your work. For kitchens, bathrooms, and other remodel jobs, a few clear photos do a lot of the convincing.
signals.next: On your next few jobs, with the homeowner's okay, snap a couple of photos and add them to the Google listing once it exists.

signals.note: We didn't find a website for BME General Remodels. For an owner-run remodel shop that's normal, but it means Nextdoor is your only home online. A Google listing can cover most of what a small website would.
signals.next: Start with the Google listing and use your Nextdoor page as its website link, so searchers can see what neighbors say. A simple one-page site can wait until you want it.

signals.note: Your phone and Lemon Grove location are consistent on Nextdoor, and we left the street off this page. The name itself isn't quite settled: the page says BME General Remodels, your own story says BME General Construction, and one reply says BME General remodels Inc. With no Google listing yet, there isn't a second public listing to compare against.
signals.next: Pick one spelling of the name and use it everywhere, including Google. Set the Google listing up as a service-area business so a home address stays private, and keep the same name, number, and service area in both places.
